interface.title: BioT - Bioinformatics Tools
interface.stage_of_work: Early exploratory analysis of sequence data, after getting sequences and before detailed alignment or annotation
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a FASTA file and either summarise the nucleotide or amino-acid composition of chosen records (counts, frequencies, GC content, chi-square uniformity test) or compare two records with a windowed dotplot.

data.note: I used the bundled examples ls_orchid.fasta (many orchid ITS records), sars-cov-2-replicase-after-alignments.fa (protein records) and homo-sapiens-tnf-after-alignments.txt (TNF mRNA records from several species). I also uploaded the test file SARS-CoV-2_complete_genome.fasta (one record, MW681002.1, 30146 nt). Each load showed 'File correctly uploaded. Validation successfully completed.' and the box 'File currently cached: <name>'. Loading a new file replaces the cached one. The uploaded file stays listed in the uploader even after an example replaces it in the cache.

features.name: Session dataset loader with example picker and cache status
features.general: Bring in a data file either by uploading your own or picking a bundled sample. It is validated, held for the session, and a status box always names the file in use. Loading another file replaces it.
features.specific: In the sidebar, 'Upload a FASTA file' plus 'Upload a file', or 'Or choose an example' plus 'Upload an example file'. Shows 'File correctly uploaded. Validation successfully completed.' and 'File currently cached: <name>'. Both tool pages then list that file's record IDs.
steps: Browse for a file (FASTA/FA/TXT) or pick an example from the dropdown
Press the matching upload button
Read the validation message
Check the 'File currently cached' box. The record lists on both pages now come from this file.
serves_tasks: Choose the pair of sequences to compare

features.name: Multi-select of records with one collapsible report per record
features.general: Pick several items from a list. Each becomes its own collapsible report panel, in the order picked, so you can compare them one after another.
features.specific: In the 'Select one or more sequences for analysis' multiselect, each chosen record ID adds an expander titled with the ID. Remove one with its chip ×.
steps: Open the multiselect and choose a record
Add more records. Each adds an expander below.
Expand (+) or collapse (−) each record's panel
Remove a record with its chip ×
serves_tasks: View counts and frequencies of each symbol in a table and a bar chart

features.name: Composition profile with uniformity test
features.general: For one item, count each symbol and show observed against expected-uniform frequency in a table and an interactive bar chart. Then give a summary ratio and a chi-square goodness-of-fit verdict against a uniform distribution. Check that the summary ratio makes sense for the kind of sequence, and note that p is rounded.
features.specific: Inside a record expander: record name and length, a table (Count, Frequency %, Exp. frequency % = 25 for DNA or 5 for protein, Diff in frequencies), a Plotly bar chart of counts with hover tooltips, 'GC content: x%', and 'The sequence is (not) homogeneous (χ²(df) ≈ …; p ≈ …)'. GC content is also printed for protein records, where it counts the amino acids G and C and means nothing (15.417% for R1AB_SARS2). p is shown rounded, so very small values read 'p ≈ 0.0'.
steps: Expand a record
Read the distribution table
Hover bars in the count chart for exact values
Read GC content (nucleotide records only)
Read the chi-square homogeneity verdict
serves_tasks: View counts and frequencies of each symbol in a table and a bar chart
Report the share of G and C bases
Test whether the symbols occur in equal proportions

features.name: Windowed dotplot comparison of two sequences
features.general: Pick two items, or the same item twice to look for internal repeats, and a match-length window. Then build a scatter of positions where the two share an exact stretch. Diagonal runs mark shared regions, and changing the window trades sensitivity against noise.
features.specific: Choose the first and second sequence. Both lists hold only the records of the cached file, so both must come from one file, and the page says it is for nucleotide sequences. Set 'Enter the window value' (number input with −/+, minimum 5) and press Generate dotplot. It shows 'N unique matches' and a Plotly scatter with both axes labelled with the record ID and its length in bp. Changing any input clears the plot ('Not enough data') until you regenerate.
steps: Choose the first sequence
Choose the second sequence (the same one for a self-comparison)
Set the window value by typing or with −/+
Press Generate dotplot and read the match count
Change the window or the pair and regenerate to compare
serves_tasks: Compare a sequence with itself to find internal repeats
Choose the pair of sequences to compare
Set the match-length threshold and build the comparison plot
Inspect diagonal runs to locate shared regions

features.name: Zoomable interactive chart with coordinate hover and PNG export
features.general: Explore a dense chart. Drag a box to zoom into a region, hover a point to read its values, double-click to reset, go fullscreen, and save the view as an image.
features.specific: The Plotly chart toolbar, used here mainly on the dotplot: drag a box to zoom, hover a point for 'seqA (length L bp)=i / seqB (length L bp)=j', double-click to zoom back out, use the View fullscreen button, and press the camera icon to download newplot.png. The composition bar chart is also a Plotly chart; only its hover tooltip was tried.
steps: Drag a box over a region of interest
Hover points to read their values
Double-click to reset the zoom
Open fullscreen for a larger view
Press the camera icon to save a PNG
serves_tasks: View counts and frequencies of each symbol in a table and a bar chart
Inspect diagonal runs to locate shared regions

screens_never_reached: A failed-validation state for a malformed or non-FASTA upload: I had no invalid test file to give it.
Dotplot of protein records: the page says it is for nucleotide sequences, and I did not try amino-acid records there.
not_done: I did not try the Plotly pan, lasso, box-select, autoscale and spike-line modes on either chart. I only tried box-zoom, hover, double-click reset, fullscreen and PNG export.
I did not load homo-sapiens-beta-globin-region.fasta, as an example or from the test files.
I did not open the Wikipedia and tutorial links on the Two Sequence Alignment page because they point off the allowed server.
I did not run a dotplot of the 30 kb SARS-CoV-2 genome against itself. It is the file's only record, and a 30146×30146 comparison could stall the server.
There is no way to download the composition table or the chi-square result. Only the Plotly charts can be saved, as PNG.
Note on results: 'GC content' is also reported for protein records (15.417% for R1AB_SARS2). It seems to count the amino acids G and C, so the number means nothing for proteins (screens/041.webp).
Note on results: the window value cannot go below 5. The − button was disabled at 5 (screens/025.webp).

open_fixes: The dotplot refusal of non-A/C/G/T records ('The nucleotide sequence was not introduced') was never reached. A new run should try a protein or ambiguous-base record on the dotplot page to capture the error and add the input-type guard feature.

That the dotplot finds only exact same-strand matches (no reverse complement, so inversions are missed) comes from the code, not the run. A new run should compare a sequence with its reverse complement to show it.

The invalid or non-FASTA upload error ('Error while processing a file...') and the 'No file selected.' error were not reached. A new run needs a malformed file, and should press upload with no file chosen.
The Home page and the bundled help PDF were never captured in kept screens. A new run should visit and screenshot them (minor).
Zoom and other toolbar modes on the composition bar chart were not tried, so f5's reuse there rests only on the hover tooltip. A new run could confirm them.
